sections.html:
Lee County property tax runs through two desks. Call the appraiser at 239-533-6100 about worth, exemptions and the address where mail goes. Call the collector at 239-533-6000 about paying.

The split matters at closing. The collector cannot change a value or an exemption, and the appraiser accepts no payments. A special assessment for roads, fire, water or sewer belongs to the authority that levied it, and its contact details are printed on the tax bill.

  • Appraiser: parcel records, value, exemption files, mailing address.
  • Collector: bills, receipts, quarterly and partial payment plans, deferral.
  • Clerk: deed recording, stamp tax, and petitions in value disputes.

Bills open for payment on November 1 and are due by March 31 of the following year. A balance still unpaid on April 1 is delinquent.

The statewide early-pay scale begins at 4 percent off in November and falls a point each month through February, so March payments earn nothing. Lenders sometimes still appear on a notice after the loan is paid off; the collector says that does not block the November discount.

Every city in the county follows this single calendar, from Cape Coral to Sanibel. There are six ways to pay: web, phone, mail, in person, kiosks, and 24-hour lockers at four centers. Late tax calls for more secure funds than a personal check or eCheck, so arrange certified money ahead of any closing.

sections.h2: Payment plans from the Lee County Tax Collector
sections.html:
Three options exist: quarterly installments, partial payments and homestead deferral. The installment application closes first.

Lee County payment plans at a glance
PlanApplyMain rule
Quarterly installmentsBy April 30 of the tax year (applications open November 1)Estimated tax must exceed $100 per notice; payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31
Partial paymentsNovember 1 to March 31Up to five payments per account; none online; no discounts
Homestead deferralBy March 31Age, income and lien rules apply; deferred tax becomes a lien and fire insurance is required

Installment discounts start at 6 percent on the first payment, drop to 4.5 percent, then 3 percent, and disappear on the last. Miss the first payment past July 31 and enrollment ends. Partial payments cover only the current tax year, never delinquent tax, and an owner already on installments cannot combine the two.

Selling partway through the year does not cancel the plan, because the incoming owner carries it to year end. Tell the closing agent early.

Homestead removes the first $25,000 of assessed value for every levy. A second amount, up to $26,411 for 2026 as the appraiser prints it, applies only to non-school levies on value above $50,000.

Form DR-501 is due to the appraiser by March 1. Send it online at leepa.org, by email to exemptions@leepa.org, by mail to PO Box 1546, Fort Myers, FL 33902, or drop it off at 2480 Thompson Street, 4th Floor, Fort Myers, on weekdays during business hours. Processing wraps up by July 1. The Save Our Homes cap on yearly assessment growth begins the year after the exemption is granted.

Each Lee taxing body sets its own senior exemption for income-qualified owners aged 65 and over:

  • City of Sanibel, City of Bonita Springs and City of Fort Myers: $25,000.
  • City of Cape Coral: $50,000.
  • Town of Fort Myers Beach and Village of Estero: $50,000 and up to $250,000.
  • All Lee County millages: $50,000 and up to $250,000.

The appraiser also lists exemptions for disabled veteran owners, disabled first responders, surviving spouses and deployed service members, plus $5,000 exemptions for widows, widowers, blind owners and others with disabilities. Most renew every January 1 unless ownership or residency changes.

sections.h2: What happens to homestead when you sell?
sections.html:
Nothing carries over automatically. A buyer must apply fresh, and the seller's exemption falls away at the next turn of the year.

A TRIM notice that shows homestead in the year of purchase still reflects the seller's benefit, which will be removed. Renting the property long term, or changing how title is held through certain trusts or LLCs, can also end the exemption, and the office wants to hear about any change in ownership.

A seller moving to another Florida home must apply again at the new address for homestead and for the Save Our Homes portability benefit. The state rule gives a three-year window counted from January 1 of the year the old homestead was given up, using Form DR-501T by March 1.

TRIM is the appraiser's preview, mailed in mid-August. The bill comes from the collector, generally in November, and it is the actual charge. It is also the only document that lists non-ad valorem items like garbage, fire or water.

The notice displays market value, exemptions, Save Our Homes status and proposed tax. Dispute a value with the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of the notice. A denied exemption has a separate 30 days from the denial letter. Keep both papers handy for buyers who ask what the house costs to carry.

On Amendment 3, the collector's FAQ says it begins January 1, 2027 and leaves the 2026 bill alone. Millage varies by address across school, city and district levies, so use your parcel lookup and your own notice instead of a countywide average.

sections.h2: Who pays Lee County tax at a sale?
sections.html:
The closing agent splits the year between buyer and seller on the settlement statement. The bill itself still goes to the owner of record when the roll reaches the collector, so a former owner may receive one.

If that happens, pass it to the new owner or the closing agent. A transfer is recorded with the clerk and then relayed to the appraiser, so some lag is normal. Unpaid tax appears in the title search and is cleared from the seller's funds.

Lee County deeds carry the standard Florida stamp rate, 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and Miami-Dade differs. Each party to the deed answers for it, and the clerk takes payment at recording.

Lee County lies on the Gulf Coast with about 875,607 residents, up 15.1 percent from 2020. Of 479,540 housing units, 74.3 percent are owner-occupied, and the typical home value for 2020 to 2024 is $362,200. Residents 65 and over are 29.2 percent of the population, which is why the senior exemptions above come up so often in sales.

The municipalities are Cape Coral, Fort Myers, Bonita Springs, Estero, Sanibel and Fort Myers Beach. Owners outside those limits sit in unincorporated areas billed by the same two offices.

sections.h2: Getting ready to sell: a short checklist
sections.html:
1. Look up your parcel with the appraiser and check the owner name and mailing address.
  2. Ask the collector for a current balance and whether any year is delinquent.
  3. If you are on installments, get a list of the payments already made and hand it to the closing agent.
  4. Gather your TRIM notice and last tax bill for buyers who ask about carrying costs.
  5. Decide where your next homestead will be so you can plan the portability filing.

A cash buyer skips lender underwriting, but the title search still turns up unpaid tax, so these papers matter on that route too.

faqs.q: Is Lee County property tax due on the same dates every year?
faqs.a: Yes. Bills open November 1, are due March 31, and turn delinquent April 1. The discount shrinks from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February.

faqs.q: Can I still join the Lee County installment plan after April 30?
faqs.a: No. The window runs November 1 to April 30, and a late applicant is limited to the partial payment plan, open through March 31.

faqs.q: Does the buyer get my homestead exemption in Lee County?
faqs.a: No. Buyers apply on their own. A TRIM notice showing homestead right after a purchase carries the seller's old benefit, which gets removed.

faqs.q: Whom should I contact if my Lee County value looks wrong?
faqs.a: Phone the appraiser at 239-533-6100. A formal petition on a DR-486 form goes to the clerk within 25 days of the proposed-tax notice.

faqs.q: What happens if Lee County property tax is unpaid when I sell?
faqs.a: The title company clears it from your funds, along with added charges. Personal checks and eChecks are refused for late tax, so ask the collector which funds it takes.
